Absolutely amazing. teaches well and exams are fair. I do wish he had recorded his lectures as missing a class can be difficult, however the main points, slides, etc. are beyond helpful. 10/10 lecturer and person.

Prof Krishnan is really sweet, I love her. It’s easy to succeed because she records lectures and provides us good resources. Our exams are content heavy and pretty specific compared to other profs but she provides a study guide, so it’s easy to study efficiently.

At first took a bit to get use to her accent, but she a very sweet lady and doesn't want this course to be a weed out class, her exams are pulled straight out of lecture slides and are very easy if you study the material. I went to office hours 2-3 times and she was super helpful. 10/10 recommend.

Don't look at the bad reviews they were the ones that didn't study, she is super friendly and sweet and her exams are pulled straight out of lecture slides. She really wants you to pass, answers emails quickly and very approachable in office hours. 10/10 recommend.

In this 100-level class, the professor seems to expect a level of understanding beyond what's typical for an entry-level course. I initially felt confident about taking the class despite my limited biology background, but that confidence quickly fell after the first exam. The professor's lecture slides are overwhelming, with over 50 slides per session, and there's no assistance provided in terms of study guides. While the group study sessions (GSS) are available, they aren't much help because the professor doesn't provide previous exams to the leaders, leaving them to guess at what might be covered.

The exams themselves delve far too deeply into the material, assuming a level of prior knowledge in biology and chemistry that many students, including myself, don't possess. Despite a significant portion of the class struggling and the average grade dropping, the professor used a student who scored exceptionally well as evidence that everyone should be able to succeed. However, it's unrealistic to use the success of a few students to dismiss the challenges faced by the majority. Additionally, the professor offers a slight reprieve by dropping one out of the three exams, while this is very helpful it's evident that this gesture falls short of addressing the fundamental issue. Even with this help, the lack of extra credit or a curve, as stated clearly in the syllabus, exacerbates the situation. I have talked with a few classmates and they feel the same. Overall he teaches the class way too hard for an intro-level class. AVOID AT ALL COST!!!!!!!!!!
I'm lowkey a bad student but he's a really good lecturer so definitely take his class. His slides are clear and he chooses really really good TAs who are super helpful. I love the group activities.

Great lecturer. Easy points in the class with the homework quizzes (untimed, but only 1 submission opportunity), worksheets, and clicker questions (for completion, not accuracy). His exams reflect exactly what he puts on the important points document for each exam. He posts all slides on ELMS. If you do your work and study for exams, you'll be just fine. He's a nice guy, too.

Keller is great and takes time to break the concepts down into really simple pieces. Exams can be difficult and you definitely need to study to do well, but he gives you all the information you need. As long as you go to class, take notes on lectures, and complete the worksheets, you will do well.

He is such a sweet professor and always worked hard to make sure his students understand material. As for his exams, they are easy if you pay attention to the information he says. They are made based off of the powerpoint slides, his own major points document that is paired with the powerpoint slides, and clicker questions. He is very passionate and friendly. Clicker questions are used as extra credit and homework worksheets help with understanding material on the exam. He prepares you well to succeed in the class.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. The exams do not match the content mentioned in exam reviews and the class is incredibly harder than any other bsci170 course that other professors teach. He expects us to know everything and treats us as if we are upper biology students. He does not listen to students when we share our need pass this INTRO level course. He drops the lowest exam grade but with our exam averages being no more than a 70% IT DOES NOTHING. More than half the class is struggling with this course. Most sitting at 70% or lower. I would never recommend another student to take this professor. The amount of stress this class has caused me is unreal. Studying hours and hours just to bomb exams is highly disappointing. My current grade DOES NOT reflect the amount of effort, time, energy, etc that I have put into this class. Please take another professor and take these reviews seriously.

Dr. Krishnan is super sweet. She’s a really nice and undrstanding professor. The exams are easy as long as you study the PowerPoints. To be honest, sometimes she explains concepts in a confusing way, but she’s more than willing to implement feedback and answer additional questions. She also hosts exam review sessions and provides a study guide.

fletcher seems like a nice guy but overall this class was way more stressful than it needed to be. lectures were long and overwhelmed with information that could all be asked on the exam, and very few of the key concepts were actually explained. no study guides or any review for anything, including the final. unless you have a decent background in biology you WILL struggle in this class, it is not beginner/major requirement friendly at all. all of my friends who took keller did significantly better and weren't as lost as I was. take keller.

Dr fletcher is very nice and accommodating. I usually skip his lectures and he records them all and posts the slides for me to take notes later. About once a week there is a group activity where attendance is required and you complete a worksheet in class. There are concept checks after every lecture but you have 3 attempts. There are 3 unit exams (one is dropped) and one cumulative final. I would recommend staying on top of notes as the class does move fast and using the practice exam guides he gives to study..
DO NOT TAKE HIM FOR BSCI170. Teaches like an upper level bio class, gives no exam help, and does not curve even though the averages for all 3 exams were under a 70%.

Good professor who sticks to what you need to know. I highly recommend showing up to lecture because you get significant extra credit just for attempting (you don't even need the right answer) clicker questions. Never talked to him but he seemed friendly. The work he assigns was relevant and genuinely helpful for learning the material, instead of being busywork. Additionally, I thought that the exams were very fair, especially since the study guides covered what you needed to know. If you need to take 170 I'd recommend him!

Professor Haag. Where to start? Tbh, I absolutely do not understand any of the hate he gets. The lectures are pretty much as straightforward as they can be for cell bio, he has an engaging way of speaking and seems interested in teaching the class, so it's not horrifically boring. I admit to loving bio, but going to his lectures was usually the highlight of the days on which I had five lectures in a row. Anyways, he offers an insane amount of free points which are pretty much all completion, yes some of them require actually going to lecture but whatever. Most lectures you could get away with not going to/paying attention, especially because he always posted the full lecture notes before class, so you could just use those. Also super helpful and kind when you reach out to him, he's willing to spend time with you to explain concepts. Exams were mad easy, I never got less than 90%, many multiple choice questions would have up to 2 bogus answer options ("what kind of bond holds DNA base pairs together?" "james bonds" etc.) which would make things easier, often the answer to one question was in the question of another, and then bonus questions that were unmissable (2pts for "which umd basketball team made it to tournament this year again?" "the women's" "not the men's"). Yes, there's no curve. You really, really shouldn't need one if you can handle a tiny bit of memorization and can understand some systems, maybe a little understanding of greek roots would be helpful too, but flashcards would do instead also. Dr. Haag is just so earnest and friendly, would definitely recommend.

Shes new so give her a break. Compared to other BSCI170 classes, this is downright the easiest class omg. Just review her slides constantly like for 30 minutes a week or so and easy B+. Her double weekly quizzes can be a pain but its whatever. Just saying if you're a stem major and you take chem131 before this you will definitely do good. She curves hellllllaaa. She does have worksheets are can be kinda annoying but their alright tbh their open note and open internet so uh skill issue tbh. Also she really does try to help and shes very kind. Her lectures are a waste of time through in my opinion, I would just self study the course.

Okay so a lot of the first reviews come from the first half of the semester, which is (sort of) fair. I never thought she was awful, but things were definitely a lot harder. However, I think she is a good prof because she actually took the time to listen and improve what she was doing. Without that, I know I would've failed this class entirely so I don't think she deserves the hate, but if you're bad at stuff like BSCI you may have to work at this class a little. I am terrible with anything science related, hence the grade, so sometimes lectures were a little fast for me and others. After some feedback she put out study guides that were near identical to exams so if you just studied you could get passable grades even if it isn't your thing. She just seemed to not know where people were at education-wise when starting, but she really didn't want to fail anyone or to try and make things difficult. She's sweet and a good listener, so I think her next semesters teaching will be a lot better than the initial one. I wouldn't let the bad reviews scare me from taking her class.

Good guy, easy class. He posts all his slides so you never actually have to go to lecture, but do because he makes funny jokes and it makes him feel better when he actually sees class engagement. Overall this class is very easy with Keller, and his exams are straightforward and never try to trick you. He is very honest and tells you exactly what he expects of you, if you actually try this class will be a breeze and you'll end up enjoying some of his dad jokes.

I want to start off with I do not recommend this professor. The work he provides is concept checks after each lecture, which are relatively easy points. Then pre-quiz GAE which is also easy. Lastly, the worksheet GAEs are mainly based on participation. When it comes to him reviewing the lectures in class he reads off the slides and does not explain it well. He has made it clear that the class average for midterms and the final were extremely low. Compared to the students in Keller, where they are actually being taught in each lecture and have a higher grade average. The attendence for lectures is not mandatory, but the GAE sessions are. He is a nice person, but not a good professor if you are trying to learn and pass. I recommend you to take keller if you want to pass and learn better.

Dr. Keller is an amazing professor. The only bad things that are not bad at all is that he doesn't record lectures and he does not have a curve. Attendance isn't mandatory but I suggest that you go to class because he often does problems from homework and has clicker questions he offers as extra credit (main reason why a curve is not necessary). The grading is very fair, reasonable, and straightforward. I don't think the workload is a lot, I was finishing homework and quizzes in under an hour (the homework is based on the notes - easy). To do well on the tests, the notes that Dr. Keller posts and his summary pages are your best resource. He does not put anything on the test that he does not cover, and getting an A on exams is very doable as long as you utilize the notes. The content of the course may seem intimidating, but don't let anyone tell you it is in his class because Dr. Keller is very reasonable and teaches very well. Also, the textbook is super unnecessary, I recommend you save some money and don't buy it if you have Keller (my biggest regret - I never used it).

I had a good experience in this class. 
Pros: Tests are straightforward. Doing clicker questions in lectures gives you a good deal of extra credit. Slides are posted in ELMS. Other assignments (ELMS quizzes, worksheets) are also straightforward and good practice. Dr. Keller is a good lecturer, and makes an effort to answer questions and make sure people understand. 
Cons: The slides aren’t super informative. You should definitely attend lecture, as it’s hard to learn the content fully using only the slides. Lecture recordings are not posted.
DON'T take him. You're much better off with Keller. His lectures are too fast, confusing, and boring. Trust me.

Such a great professor! The exams were very straightforward, there were no complicated wording or round-about questions. He asked the questions straight and simple and as long as you knew the material, it was very easy to answer. He explained the concepts in class simply as well, overall as a teacher he made sure not to overcomplicate things. 
He also assigned a lot of homework worksheets, but only the top five are put into the gradebook. Go to class for these!! He literally goes over the entire worksheet in-class step by step, at that point he nearly gives you the answer key for the worksheets. He also assigns weekly elms quizzes which are open note and can be completed outside of class. They are all two attempts, and they are a great way to review your understanding. There are four midterms and one final, which sounds like a lot initially, but the first midterm is only 60 points. It is a good way to get started in the semester, and this extra midterm makes the final weigh less since it is only out of 140 points instead of the typical 200. 
Dr. Keller makes sure this class is simple to understand, since he understands that this class is still at a general level. He remarks often in class that he is teaching these concepts very simply and if you go to higher level BSCI courses they will go more in depth. So this may not be the best teacher if you want an indepth understanding early on to better prepare you for higher level BSCI courses. But this is definitely a good teacher to take for BSCI170 if you want a good and general introduction to cell biology!!
Dr. Krishnan’s class is easy as long as you review her study guides. She’s super sweet and is always willing to help or answer any clarifying questions.

DO NOT TAKE 170 WITH THIS PROFESSOR!!!!! Yes, Dr. Haag is very nice; you can tell he loves bio. But his exams make no sense whatsoever. You can study all of the slides, just for him to throw a curveball on the exam. His average exam scores are between 50-69%. You can't retake the exams. Rather, he has you write a written explanation for the questions you got wrong and explain why you deserve more points. It doesn't boost your grade either. His only advice for failing exams is "study harder". Expect to study for 2 hours + each night just to try to get at least a 70 on one of the exams. Each unit has 4-6 chapters in it, and you have to memorize 50-60+ slides for each chapter. He doesn't curve exams. The TAs even stated that his tests were too challenging for a 170 class. I sent out an email stating that our final exam grades were 6% worse than the scores from his 170 sessions the previous semester. Then, at the end of the email, he said that those who got less than a C just "didn't understand the material". This class ruined my GPA, please don't take this professor.

I would like to preface, that Dr. Krishnan just started teaching for the first ever this semester. She is pretty nice and approachable, she does have a bit of an accent, but you will get used to it. While there were bumps in the road, she was very willing to take feedback and implement it. We did not get any sort of review guide for the first exam, but once it was suggested, she gave it to us for the rest of the exams and finals. For me, I did not find her lecturing style too helpful, as she tended to go through material fast and go on rants. She also expected us to have a lot more background info than we did, which led to awkward long pauses after she asked us questions, expecting us to know the answers. Her powerpoints come straight from the book, so if the material does not make sense I recommend going to youtube for further explanation. She really did try to engage us, though, plus she recorded and posted all lectures and review sessions. 

Quizzes (23 of them, lowest 2 dropped) are online and have a 20-30 minute time limit. Worksheets are in class, but you can work with other people and use notes, which is a grade boost. Hint: If you want to get an A you have to know the sequential steps and visual representations of ALL the processes!! I did not study these as much, and that is why I received an A- instead of an A. There are three exams and the final. The final was almost all repeat questions from exams 1-3 so a nice way to boost your grade. If you want to do really well, I would go to her for office hours! I could not due to other class conflicts, yet I still managed an A minus. In conclusion, if Keller is full she is not a bad alternative but be prepared to study outside of lecture to get the grade you want.

This guy is awesome. Absolutely the best professor at UMD… Extra credit helps a ton (I had a 100% the majority of the semester). Go to class, do some studying, and try your best and you will easily get an A. TAKE THIS GUY

I am not a STEM person and was really nervous about this class at first, but Keller taught everything I needed to know to do well on the exams. You do not need a background in bio or chem (I certainly did not have one) as everything comes straight from his lectures and study guides. You will definitely have to prepare well for exams, but an A is achievable as long as you attend class (not recorded) and study directly from the course material. I would also recommend attending GSS and office hours if you can. The online textbook is $50, but you do not need it to understand or do well on exams. The only content tested on exams is that which was discussed in lecture.

Very nice and empathetic. His BSCI170 is disorganized. Studying is a hassle, but the exams are fair and the worksheets are simple. Do not rely on this professor for dates use the course calendar! I missed a few dates, so be on top of that.

He records all his lectures and his exams were always fair. I actually never attended lecture and just rewatched the recorded lectures and so obviously my midterm grades were like 70%-80% since I didn't actually study. The concept checks and group activities saved my grade and I realized that it was already the final and I had to pull my crap together. I crammed and pulled through with a 95%. So overall, the class isn't that hard and you can cram but it'll be so much easier if you just go to lecture and take some notes here and there. The exams did have extra credit which was like 'draw your favorite animal' so you can get easy points there.

Fletcher truly is the best proessor for BSCI170. His lectures are always recorded, so as long you're paying a bit of attention in class then review using the videos, you'll do great. The exams were a bit more difficult ngl, it wasn't because the topics were hard to understand, it was just because there was so much to keep track of, he may quiz u on anything. I loved the GSS sessions, if I had gone, I'd probably have done better but my ego told me I'd be off studying on my own DO NOT BE LIKE ME. His exams are out of 80 pts and there's 3 of them, he drops the lowest score tho. The first and second exams seemed to have been the easiest, I had gotten sick and didn't get to make up the second one because I contacted him too late (he didn't let me retake it because he drops one of the exams), again, DO NOT BE LIKE ME. Contact him early and definitely take the first 2 exams if you can, the third one was the hardest. I got a 67/80 for my 1st exam and a 62/80 for my second and I did actually try unlike the commentor on 08/07/2024. I got an 86/100 on the final since I didn't study the 2nd unit thoroughly (and I recently had a close relative passing away at the time). So pls, try your best. Keep a healthy bit of anxiety in you and don't have an inflated ego like me. 

Tip: Buy an ipad/tablet, download the lecture slides and take notes on your ipad/tablet, then you won't have to scramble to take notes AND pay attention. I personally had a Samsung tablet :)

I absolutely loved her. She would meet with you one-on-one not during office hours for you to really grasp the concept. This is a hard class with a lot of memorization but she made it manageable! If you have to take this class, definitely take it with her!

Dr. Keller is such an overall great professor. He is a very chill and understanding guy and a good teacher. He broke down topics very well and had all the info you need on the slides. His tests were very fair and had similar questions to the worksheets. He also gives extra credit for clicker questions.

Dont know why people rate Dr Lin low. He truly cares for students and does well to make the class engaging. He is very funny and has great one liners. Kinda difficult class but as the semester has gone on, he has done a really good job letting us know what is the important information we need to know.

Super easy!! I did better on this than the actual lecture. The work isn't too bad. As long as your group is good, the group assignments are easy. 

I have never met the professor, you just have a TA with you the entire time. Overall it's not bad at all.
She just reads off the slides really fast. Just get ready to teach yourself everything. Textbook and youtube videos. The structure of the class isn't too bad though.

Chan is a very okay lecturer. He tries to make his lectures somewhat interesting and engaging, but his pacing was absolutely awful for the semester. We were behind on content for almost the entire semester because he keeps on yapping about stuff that he then tells us will NOT be on the exam. He rushed through the last few topics in the last few classes, so be prepared to get a study group together to learn all the content yourselves. Attend the GSSes that the TA's hold. He's an easy grader and the exams are relatively easy. You do NOT need to get the textbook, I used online resources for the most part and the slides, and that worked perfectly fine. The first exam was very bio chem heavy, but I want to blame that on the fact that it's his first time teaching the course, and he didn't know how to write a 100 lvl test.

One of my favorite professors at UMD by far! Dr. Lin is an excellent professor. He explains the topics so well, is funny, and is very reasonable when it comes to the material tested on the exams. A lot of the questions are just repeats of the weekly quizzes (which are open-note). I would recommend Dr. Lin to anyone taking BSCI170 because he makes it genuinely interesting.

She's a very nice lady, but it was her first time teaching a class, and it was obvious. She reads through slides very quickly, doesn't explain the topics well, doesn't take questions during lecture, ends lecture 20-30 minutes early and leaves right away (can't ask many questions after class). She only has one office hour once a week, so if you have questions, she's not accessible in person too often. However, she will always answer an email with an in-depth explanation to answer your question. She also has a bit of an accent that can be hard to understand at times, which makes learning the material during lecture hard. You will have to teach yourself everything. Her tests are not terrible, everything that are on the slides are fair game however. She also gives graded worksheets at random lectures, so you have to be at every lecture in case or you'll get a zero for the assignment. The key to success in her class trying to be engaged during lecture, and going through the slides on your own and blurting or writing everything on a whiteboard. Make sure you know the cellular processes well and memorize the ideas and details on the slides.

Teaches like a researcher forced to lecture

She seems pretty nice and helpful but she just hasn't done enough teaching to be good at it. 

You can count the amount of words she says per lecture that ARENT on a slide on one hand, maybe 2. 

Absolutely anything on the slideshows is fair game for exams, good and bad since they're exhaustive but there won't be any surprises

Quizes just use google.com and go to the GSS theyre pretty good for reviewing

She 100% doesn't want to teach this class at all. She is just there because she has to be but her tests are much easier than the lady who runs the lab. I did mess up badly on my 1st one but then on my other exams I got A's. You have to teach your self everything; she records her lessons and I highly recommend you watch them when studying they help a lot. Also all her tests are multiple choice. She has random worksheets but its almost always on Thursdays and she writes them in her slides for that specific class so you have a little bit of a heads up. She doesn't really answer questions and reads off the slides but her tests are only the material on the slides. She emails back fast and her responses are well written. I will say she has a very slight accent but it doesn't really impact her teaching that much. Bottom line: she is not the worst professor to take this class with THERE ARE WORSE. I would recommend her over the lady who teaches the lab 100%.

Dr. Lin is an alright professor. I can tell that he knows his material, however it sometimes feels like he assumes that we know the material too and does not thoroughly explain the material. Because of his teaching styles, I am struggling a little bit in this class. The average on his exams are a 70 but one of the exams does get dropped. He doesn't do a good job preparing for the exams. I will say that I will study all the material for only 1/3 of it to be on the exam. As a person, he cares a lot about his students and likes to make jokes every once in a while. Overall, the class itself is kinda a mess and I would not take it again.
She goes through lecture slides super fast but there isn't much work and it is pretty easy.

Dr. Keller is a really great professor. His lectures are all recorded and he posts all of the slides on ELMS. He is really knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches which makes his lectures interesting and fun. He gives extra credit opportunities during lecture and drops your lowest worksheets. As long as you pay attention to what is talked about in lecture, the tests are pretty straightforward.

There's honestly not really a reason to complain. It is evident that this is the first time he is teaching a 100 level class but he's been very lenient because of it. After seeing that our first exam average was a 72 (which honestly doesn't even seem that bad) he decided that our lowest of 3 midterms would be dropped. He makes the weekly quizzes open note and even re-uses the questions for the exams. The only gripe that I have with the course is that he likes to do random participation questions which basically acts as attendance

Dr. Keller is a GREAT professor. Everything that was on the exams were either talked about in lecture or are on his major points documents. He puts both the lecture slides and major points on canvas for you to reference as well as the recorded lectures. I was nervous about this class since I haven't taken bio since freshman year, which was mainly online, but this class has been great. He makes the content easy to understand but I would definitely look at all of his major points documents, they're very helpful. I didn't used the textbook once and wouldn't waste money on it since everything you need to know is taught in class. He also does clicker questions for extra credit, and you can earn about 15 points just from this which is pretty generous. If you're taking a bunch of difficult classes that require more attention, I highly recommend taking Keller because this class has been pretty low stress. Overall, Dr. Keller is an amazing professor and provides you with all the resources you need to be successful in the class!

Keller is a great professor and I definitely recommend him for this class. I was unsure about taking this class because of content, but he makes it easy to understand if you show up to lecture. The one thing I will say is that you need to either attend lecture or watch the recordings, because his slides can be cryptic and hard to understand without context. I LOVED that we didn't need to read the textbook for this class- the only content on the exams is what was covered in lecture so I would say grading was very fair. He also gave extra credit opportunities during lecture. 170 with Keller was definitely more bearable than the lab component.

She is a pretty horrible lecturer. It is clear she doesn't want to be there at all but she does make the lecture required (aka random worksheets). It is super quick and she acts like you should already know the information, if you didn't AP or IB biology it will be difficult. She is nice and the class is not the worst, but you WILL have to learn it completely on your own.

Let me start off by saying that Dr. Choi is a very nice person and this was her first year teaching a college-level course. She gives you opportunities to get extra help with topics covered in lectures by having guided study sessions (GSS) and office hours with her and her TA's. Compared to the other professors who teach this course, I would say that she is your best bet. If I am going to be completely transparent, she is an okay teacher. There were a couple of things that I didn't like about her class and teaching style. She reads DIRECTLY from the slides that she makes for lectures and doesn't give the class time to ask questions. Her presentations are always between 45-70 slides long and they are hard to follow because she teaches at a very fast pace. One thing she did tell us is to not rely solely on the slides that she uses to teach to study because you will not pass your exams if you do so. If you really want to do well in her class, use the textbook to study, study in advance, and watch videos on the topics that are being taught. She also made it very clear that she doesn't give extra credit or curves any grades. I will say, she is very good at answering questions in depth if you email her or talk to her directly.

Dr. Keller is amazing. He always thoroughly explains topics and often uses helpful analogies to make them easier to understand. There were 4 exams and a final, with the first exam being a "mini" exam only worth 60 points. He provides very helpful study guides as well as documents detailing the contents of each lecture in depth. He also provides clicker questions that help you earn extra credit as long as you attend lectures. He also posts lectures, and I found that going back and listening to his lectures helped me succeed on his tests. The only thing I didn't like was that a lot of his test questions are designed to trick you sometimes.

Dr. Keller is a really great professor, he recorded all of his lectures which allowed for me to skip class and take notes after the fact. He sometimes goes on random tangents or stories, but it helps break up the topics in class as he tries to be funny and relate to his students.

She is genuinely a nice lady but she does not want to teach. She is definitely here to do research and then is forced to teach this class. You have to teach yourself and study way too much for an 100 level class to do well on the exams. She reads quickly off the slides and makes weird comparisons to other things that only makes sense sometimes. I recommend going to every lecture because it forces you to read the slides. She mainly uses the slides for exams but I recommend using the textbook tests to study. As long as you do the in class worksheets and the elms quizzes you should be ok, grade wise. She speed reads the lectures and then immediately leaves. I would recommend emailing her if you have a question. You should definitely go to the GSS sessions. They are super helpful and great to have someone actually teach you

I don't know why Dr. Mohan is rated so low; she's the best professor I had this semester. She's very knowledgable about the subjects she teaches and it's clear she's genuinely passionate about biology. It's actually SO HARD to fail this class as long as you focus in class and use the resources given to you - Mohan posts the lecture slides before class and posts the recordings almost immediately after. ONE THING! Dr. Mohan does NOT mess around. She sets her expectations first day of class (don't ask to go back a slide - they're posted so it makes sense - and don't talk while she's lecturing - since there's mics all over the room and they pick up any noise). As long as you're attentive and ask good questions, she's going to like you. She's also kinda hilarious but that's besides the point. I highly recommend taking this class with Dr. Mohan; she's the best.

Her class wasn't terrible but she is not a strong lecturer. She is hard to pay attention to because she tends to just read off the slides and it can be very boring. Her tests were fine, no written answers or anything, but this is definitely a "teach yourself" kind of class. I wouldn't recommend her as a bio professor as I think this content could be very interesting and fun if the person teaching it actually seemed to enjoy it at all. Instead, Dr. Choi's lecturing style made this class a drag and I couldn't wait for it to be over.
I love Mohan so much! Her class is structured in a way that makes getting an A so easy! Definitely take her.

Professor Mohan talks way too much about things that won't even be on the exam, and while I appreciate the exam review that was provided before every exam, it was way too surface level for certain topics and did not provide equal insight into what would be on the the exam for each topic. Lectures are extremely fast paced and you WILL need to rewatch them outside of class to get detailed notes, but everything you need for exams can be found in the lectures, you honestly don't even need the textbook. I paid like 80 for it and didn't use it at all. Exams are easy if you review the weekly problem sets. I've heard mixed reviews about Dr. Mohan but she's a great professor and very knowledgeable in her field. Make sure you go to TA office hours to do well.

BEST TEACHER EVER! DO NOT LISTEN TO THE REVIEWS. She explains everything very well and has recorded lectures that you can review after class. Her tests are set up just like her problem sets so it is very easy to follow. However, her exams are not multiple choice. But she does not trick you so its really easy if you know the content.

(Disclaimer: I am a CHEM major and took Hon Biology in high school. I came in with knowledge of most of this material)

Dr. Lin was a pretty good professor. His class has three midterms and one cumulative final exam, which should all be weighted the same at 100 points. For studying I would highly recommend studying the quizzes and the one-question quizzes he gives in class, because at least one of them will show up on the exams. Exam format includes multiple choice, short answer, and fill in the blank, but they aren't too long if you know what you're doing.

My only gripe is that he made Exam #3 one week before finals week, so you have a bio midterm and then the bio final within two weeks. But he always posts recordings and the slides on ELMS. I'd still go to lecture though because of the worksheets and attendance quizzes.

He is an absolute angel. He made the class way easier than I expected it to be. I promise that if you take this class and you try, you will do well. His midterms are literally just like the study guide and he truly wants you to do well. This class was fairly easy. There are participation questions each lecture that add up over time and they are opned at different times everyday so if you dont come to lecture, you will miss it. Literally not a difficult class AT ALL!! The only main problem is how much information you're expected to memorize. Dr. Keller is an amazing professor. His exams are super fair and straightforward (no trick questions) and the study guides contain everything you need to need to know. He is a great lecturer and keeps his classes interesting. I highly recommend taking this course with him.

Dr. Keller is a great professor. He explains concepts very well and takes time in between topics to process the information. his exams are easy, I got an A+ in all of them including the final. If you took AP Bio, then this class will be a breeze. Compared to all the other BSCI170 professors, this one is the best!

I took Mohan last semester for BSCI170, and I can confidently say that she is one of, if not the best, professors I have had so far. Her class is extremely well structured. 

Every week, you have 3 in-person lecture "quizzes" for participation points (one each lecture), which are not graded on accuracy but simply completion. You're allowed to drop 10 points if I'm not mistaken (which is 5 classes, since each participation quiz is 2 points). 

Additionally, every Friday after lecture, she posts an online lecture quiz that's worth 10 points. They are all graded on accuracy, but extremely easy (either multiple choice or drop-down menu answers, NEVER open-ended). You also have 2 attempts on them, AND your 3 lowest scores get dropped. 

On top of those, you also have weekly problem sets which are done in lecture on Fridays, and they are usually just a page front and back, basically just practice problems for the material you covered in class that week. They are graded on accuracy, but you get to work with the people you sit with in lecture, AND your 3 lowest scores of those get dropped as well. Personally, with my dropped scores, I received 100 on all the lecture quizzes and problem sets throughout the semester, so as long as you show up to lecture and pay attention, the only thing you need to do is review the material for her exams.

Her exams are probably the most straightforward exams that can be. All her questions are formatted the same way they are asked on problem sets and lecture quizzes, so there's no surprises on what types of questions will be asked. None of her exams have multiple choice; it's usually a matching page, and the rest is "open-ended," which I say very loosely because it's more of labeling, or writing out things rather than explaining anything. To prepare you for the exams, she releases extra problem sets with solutions and extra lecture quizzes. 

Regarding her actual lecturing, there's nothing to say other than she has her notes and goes through them. However, she explains concepts that can be confusing in extremely simple ways and gives you an amazing understanding of the concepts behind what you learned, so everything does make sense. I always uploaded her notes onto my iPad, and just used them to annotate anything she said above what's on the actual slide, which is extremely useful when going back and doing lecture quizzes, problem sets, or studying for the exams. 

When talking about averages, her exams usually averaged mid to high 80s. However, if you pay attention, show up to lecture, and try on the weekly quizzes and problem sets, you will easily get an A on all of her exams.

I cannot recommend her more if you have no issue showing up to class and actually participating. If you slack off, your grades will reflect that, but I think she teaches extremely well, and any amount of effort will get you a good grade in her class.

he is fine i dont feel like he is a good professor though I have had to heavily rely on other classes and videos and readings to get me through this class

Most of the people leaving glowing reviews here have already learned a lot of the content in BSCI170 through AP Biology or another class. Keller is a great person, he's good at making the amount of content covered in this class less daunting. But, he has a few fundamental problems that need to be addressed.

There are 5 exams total, including a cumulative final exam at the end. No curves, no dropped exams. The midterms are difficult if you are at all unfamiliar with a concept. It's hard to fully master everything given the density of the course content, and a lot of the time the topics the exams focus on are not equivalent to what Keller spends a lot of time discussing in class. There are matching questions which can be worth up to 20% of your exam grade (good luck if you get one pair wrong!), and a lot of open-ended questions with diagrams with unclear arrows to label.

Yes, having 5 midterms can help cushion you if you mess up on one. But, with more midterms comes more opportunities to have a bad day, which Keller does not account for. As I stated before, they are very dense, and one is even during the second week of the semester. 

I enjoyed the lectures Keller gave, but at times it was difficult to pick out what is important to know for the exams. He gets caught up in a lot of niche details mostly because he is very passionate about Biology. I personally like because I find it interesting, but to most people it can turn out to be pretty distracting.

Exam prep materials were sparse, only 10 multiple choice questions which were nowhere near the difficulty of the exam questions. He provides a nice list of key points from each class, and worksheets to complete, which are great but they only scratch the surface of what he wants you to know. Slides have a sentence or two on them if you're lucky, otherwise it is just bullet points to look at. Having the lecture recordings provided was nice, but as I mentioned earlier, he can gloss over important information at times in favor of other things he finds interesting.

Overall, my best advice for taking this course is to have a strong background in chemistry and be prepared to do a lot of self-studying for exams if you don't know a ton about Biology already. Keller is very approachable (when I have been able to get ahold of him, which has at times been super difficult) so try to talk to him if you are struggling.

His exams are difficult and no matter what you do, there will still be something on there that you did not study. He also offered no study guide or review whatsoever for the final. We had to try to cram everything into our brains without knowing what we were actually going to need for the final. There's no reason he cannot give a list of topics covered on the final. I wish I never took his class.

Dr. Haag is a kind and approachable professor, but I found his teaching style to be challenging for an entry-level biology course. The exams are heavily weighted, and while there are in-class worksheets and concept checks that offer “free points,” they don’t do much to support your grade if you struggle on the exams. He does drop the lowest midterm, which is helpful, but there’s no curve, and the final exam is cumulative, which makes it difficult to recall the 25+ topics. I had to spend hours teaching the material to myself outside of class. Office hours were helpful, but overall, I think more structured support or review opportunities would have made the course more manageable. If you're someone who likes independent studying, you might be fine, but if you prefer more guided instruction and balanced grading, this class may be tough.

Keller is a great guy and an excellent professor. Those who say he isn't good clearly haven't taken a class that requires a lot of studying.  Yes, his lectures can be a bit slow at times, but you will learn everything you need to know for the exams through his lectures since his slides don't give a lot of info. But he posts a lecture video after each lecture, so you can get away with not having to show up. He does not give any curveball questions, and everything you need to know will be in the worksheets, quizzes, practice exams, or the major points. The major points docx is something that I wish all my professors would do. Yes, having four exams and a final is a lot, but honestly, his exams are relatively simple/straightforward; there was never a time when I got to the exam and there was something he didn't teach. Yes, the worksheets can get hard, but he only keeps the top 5, and we did around 10 of them, and all the practice exams you get 2 tries. I feel that as long as you pay attention and put in a little bit of studying and take advantage of his exam review study guide, you should do pretty well.

Dr. Keller is an amazing professor. I love the simplicity of his lecture slides because they give me the chance to take my notes and write down what he says in lecture into my own words. He also records and posts, which is helpful if you ever miss a class. He also gives clicker questions as extra credit, which will help you out a lot at the end of the semester. He is very understanding and lenient with his grades. For example, he gives you about a 3-day extension on the weekly quizzes if you accidentally miss the Friday deadline (happened to me once, and I was panicking). Although he doesn't curve the course/drop an exam, the extra credit, homework assignments, and weekly quizzes make up for it. His exams are extremely fair, and his lectures/homework truly prepare you for the class. I never got below a 92% on an exam (including the final). His positivity radiates into this class, and it's obvious that he truly loves what he teaches. Definitely recommend taking him!!! You WILL NOT regret it.

Definitely the easiest science class I’ve ever taken. Didn’t take AP bio in high school and only had to spend 3 hours per exam writing down each term that was necessary to memorize. Exams are extremely straight forward as long as you memorize the definition of the terms he gives on the study guide you’re guaranteed an A. Final was a little bit more conceptual so u had to understand everything a little bit more but he only gave us information on exam 3 and up for it. Also he gives 20 extra credit points for showing up to class. Overall really lectures were kinda boring but he gives u the major points you need to know on a pdf anyways, midterms were extremely easy, homework’s and quizzes were free points, final was a little harder, but overall an easy A.

Ms. Choi is a very sweet lady she definitely just reads off the slides when she lectures but compared to other bio 170 teachers I would consider her to be easier. Her slides are very straight forward and you can easily teach the information to yourself. The midterms are very straight forward. No written response, only multiple choice true false and fill in blank/ diagram. There are online quizzes and problem sets as well as weekly worksheets that really cushion your grade. As long as you attend lecture and study the reviews before the exam you will be fine. I honestly really recommend her for bsci 170. She also ended up dropping our lowest midterm or allowing us to get extra credit points.

Very sweet professor and is helpful when you ask her questions. You have to teach yourself but that wasn’t really an issue for me personally. If you put the effort in you’ll definitely do fine in the class.

professor is cool and very nice you can tell he loves teaching, but his teaching style is just reading from 60+ slides. (Not very effective) Even with going to office hours and studying outside of class, this “intro” class is very challenging in comparison to the other professors teaching it. I would recommend if you can just waiting until another professor is available.

This review is definitely going to be biased because I do not like bio or really any sciences. Dr. Keller though is a really nice guy and very understanding and accommodating. He wants you to succeed and love the course material and think that it is as fascinating as he does. He also makes himself available outside of class for any questions and encourages you to seek the TA's help as well. If you need to take this course, I would definitely take it with him. The content in this course is very straightforward and he posts the notes and records each lecture- so you technically don't need to show up. However, he provides clicker questions, where you scan a QR code, which are bonus participation points for attending class so I would recommend you show up. Besides this there are worksheets and mini quizzes weekly to test your understanding of the material. The exams are again pretty straightforward and they test you on the main concepts of the units, he also makes study guides for each exam (of which there are 5) that help you to study. If you do not have a science brain like I do, learning this content and trying to memorize and study it can be very tedious. All you can really do is try your best in this class, take good notes, and show up to class for extra credit participation points. That being said, I would never want to take this course again lol.

I liked him, but not as much as people say. He is a nice guy, but going to his lectures was beyond pointless, except for the fact that he gives extra credit through clicker questions. As someone who isn't a science person, I still felt this course was so easy. His exams were soooo straight forward, which was great, but sucked if you didn't study something because there is not much room to fudge your way to the right answer (his exams are mostly multiple choice, fill in the blank, and labeling diagrams). 

Easy class, easy prof, brownie points for extra credit, take him, he's a fine guy. Just use all the resources he gives you because a lot of the exam questions are IDENTICAL to the practice problems he gives you.

okay ... I got an A in this class, but it wasn’t easy. I would only recommend taking it if you’re willing to study on your own and already have some background in biology.

The lectures can be tough to follow—his slides are long and sometimes hard to understand, and his voice is very monotone, which made it difficult for me to stay focused. What worked for me was sitting in the front of the class and passively listening—he does drop hints about what will be on the exam. I didn’t take extensive notes during lecture, just jotted down key things I needed to review more deeply later.

After class, I would go through the slides on my own, take detailed notes, and turn those notes into flashcards. A few days before the exam (or the night before), I’d focus on what I still didn’t know and “dump” everything I could onto a whiteboard. That strategy worked for me, but of course, it may not work for everyone.

A few other things to note:
- He goes more in-depth than other professors, so be prepared to dive deep into the material.
- He is very passionate about biology, and that comes through more in office hours. If you’re struggling or curious, go—he’ll explain things in more depth (though he tends to ramble).
- Do the practice exams—they were very similar to the real ones and super helpful.
- Definitely study hard for the first exam—it might be harder than the others.

Good luck T-T

I have not taken a biology class since 10th grade, nor was I ever really good at bio to begin with, and I took Keller in the summertime, and I was scared out of my mind because I thought it was going to be a hard and difficult time. Bro, let me fucking tell you, take Keller in the summertime; it was one of the easiest fucking A's I have ever gotten, bro. He is helpful as fuck; his exams are like the practice problems, and the worksheets are like max 3 pages. Take him bruh.

Bro take Keller in the summertime. I haven't taken bio since 10th grade and let me tell you, I had a glorious time, bruh. Take him in the summer. The practice exams were helpful, he was mad helpful, and the worksheets were like max 3 pages.

Honestly, yes, he teaches the class well and it’s light work, so I would recommend people take him for BSCI170. His notes are not too complicated, he goes over concepts a lot, and he reviews what was learned in the last lecture during the next one, so it’s not overbearing. Plus, there is light homework some weeks, so there’s really no hard work outside of class. That all being said, my only critique is on his character. Michael’s voice puts most students to sleep, and it can feel a little like being talked to as if you’re in preschool. Additionally, his ego is huge. Having spoken to him one-on-one for clarification on a test answer, he got extremely defensive, and it was not handled well. So please, by all means, take him for the course—you’ll be set—just know that this teacher will not be your buddy and will pull things out of nowhere to try and keep his ego!

Dr. Keller is a really good teacher, he does his best do make the topics really easy to understand. I highly recommend taking this class in the summer, it is what I did and I got an A. He is very straightforward about what should be expected on exams. This was my first UMD class and was overall a really good experience. Highly recommend taking Dr. Keller.

Dr. Keller was a great professor for BSCI170,,, I took AP bio during freshman year of HS and scored a 2, so I was reallyyy worried, but it was honestly so straightforward. The three most important things in this class are 

1. Ditch the textbook (I read the textbook for the first midterm, and almost none of the chapters assigned were tested; I got an 84)
2. Just memorize the study guide/lecture notes (I spammed ChatGPT-generated practice tests and asked it to make tests with the notes, got 95+ every midterm after the first one)
3. Go to the lecture for free participation points (I got bumped from like a 95 to a 99.5 because of this)

Honestly, he was really passive-aggressive at times, but he was a really good lecturer regardless...

I would highly recommend not taking Professor Haag's class. BSCI170 is a pre-requisite for a lot of STEM majors but PLEASE get a different professor. He goes extremely fast through the content and teaches like he's talking to his colleagues (other people who are literally professionals in biology). If you do get stuck in his class, be prepared for teaching yourself ALL the content, considering his teaching style is just reading from slides. He's a super nice guy but if you're looking for success in the course other professors will be your best bet. If for some reason you can't get another professor, good luck...

He made 170 an easy class to get an A in, but there were a few small issues. One or two of his exam questions were related to the content but very technical, and he didn't go over a relevant example in class. Additionally, he wasn't clear about how useful the textbook was (he rarely ever used it despite recommending us to read it). However, this was made up for by the fact that he allows one exam to be dropped. He is easy to listen and pay attention to. He also is very friendly and easy to talk to. I would recommend him for 170.

Dr. Keller is great, very clear. The tests are reflective of the class and he uses familiar charts and graphs so you're never too confused. He never gets frustrated when the class is confused, just laughs and reexplains. This is the best teacher you can take for 170, you'll get an A as I did even though I went in knowing literally nothing.
Horrible professor and horrible exams. Does not curve either.
Love him :) Take him if you can!

DO NOT TAKE HER FOR BSCI170. She is very nice but does not know how to teach this class. Her lectures are very disorganized and her slides have so much information to where its impossible to take notes on. This would be fine if it was the same stuff that is on the exam but its not even close. She does not prepare you well for your exams at all and ive heard every other professor for this class is much more straightforward. There is also no DSS which all other sections have.

This prof is very passionate and such a nice guy. However he does not curve tests even when the avg is not above a 65. It can be frustrating. He luckily drops the lowest midterm grade but with little help from other assignments you have to do really well on the tests. His lectures are him reading off of a 65 page slideshow and not going in depth. If you ask for feedback on test questions his generic response is that you didn’t try hard enough. Just an overall frustrating and difficult course considering it’s supposed to be an entry level course.

Dr. Haag is a good professor! He speaks clearly and gives in-depth explanations every lecture. He also provides many opportunities for success: concept check quizzes that are extremely easy to get 100% correct, group activity worksheets that are graded on completion, and practice exams so similar to the actual ones that it's impossible to fail. Cell biology is challenging content, and he is very passionate about it so this does tend to result in occasional side-tracking into subtopics. However, attending every lecture, taking copious notes, and working hard in the class will ensure success.

She is new-- but absolutely AMAZING. I have recommended her to all my friends and am looking to take her BSCI213 course this next semester. She is super passionate, straight forward, easy to understand, really puts together everything into the slide shows. She is always open to questions and you have all the resources to do well in her class. All lectures are hosted online and in person and the slide decks are posted too. Two of your quizzes are dropped at the end of the semester. She also makes funny jokes. Take her class if you can!!

Genuinely an amazing professor, I highly recommend her. Her grades are extremely fair, her exams directly correlate to what we learn in class, and she drops the two lowest quiz grades (which are open note). She is so good at teaching and I've never understood biology better than I have when taking this course. Attendance is a grade but I'd recommend going in person anyways to get a better grasp of the material. She genuinely wants you to succeed and cares about each and every student.

Literally amazing professor. She is so good at getting you to understand the material, I've never enjoyed biology before until this class. She is also so funny so the class is actually interesting and I want to go to class.

Dr. Weiss is amazing! This was her first time teaching BSCI170, but her teaching style and class structure are incredibly succinct and helpful toward the exams. At the start of every lecture there are objectives which you should write down, cause they will most likely be on the exam. The current structure of the class is like this:
- Participation QR code questions every class (4.5% of grade)
- Weekly online quizzes (8 total, 2 worst scores dropped; 18.5% of grade)
- 4 Graded SimUText Modules (SimUText, the online textbook, costs about $50, it's the only textbook you need to buy, 6% of grade)
- 3 Midterms worth ~46% of your grade
- 1 Final worth ~23% of your grade
Show up to class, pay attention, and study the material. I ended up teaching other people with other professors because Dr. Weiss' method and diagrams were so useful. She also never puts trick questions on exams and they are pretty straight forward with multiple choice, fill in the blanks, and true or false questions.

She is an incredible teacher for BSCI170. I had her my very first semester of college and everything about her course structure was extremely helpful when adjusting to the workload. Her exams are extremely fair and she provides objectives for every lecture that serves as the perfect study guide.

On top of exams, she provides an inordinate amount of ways to earn other points in the class such as quizzes, easy graded SimBios, and participation questions-- she also posts lectures in case you miss one. I used to hate bio from high school, but after taking it with her I have a new appreciation and interest in the content she taught. Side note-- she also drops two quizzes and there are readings included for every lecture topic but you don't need to do them at all because her lecture covers all the material and she doesn't pull any trick questions on exams etc.

Besides the course itself, she's funny, sharp, and witty and the way she teaches the lectures are interesting and engaging. She cares a lot about her students and providing support when and where its needed, definitely take her over other BSCI170 profs! We had Keller step in to teach two lectures and even though he seems like a great teacher, his lecture style was very boring and his slideshows were not detailed with notes whatsoever.

Dr. Weiss is amazing! It was her first time teaching BSCI170 but her teaching style and diagrams are incredibly informative for the exams. Speaking of, her exams are extremely straight forward with multiple choice, fill in the blank, and some short answer questions (usually like 1 or 2). Her class structure goes as follows:
- Participation questions, QR codes on the slides (5% of grade, still have to show up in person)
- 8 weekly online quizzes (2 lowest scores dropped, 18.5% of grade)
- 4 Graded SimUText Modules ($50 online textbook, 6% of grade)
- 3 Midterm exams (46% of grade)
- 1 Final (23% of grade)
Show up to class, study the material, and you should be fine. She puts no trick questions and the exams are very straight forward. If you miss class, you can't do the participation question of the day but she posts the slides and records the lectures.

I LOVE Proff. Weiss. She is an absolutely amazing teacher and is very funny. I almost didn't take her because she didn't have any reviews, but thank gosh I did. The tests are very straightforward and only include material from the posted PowerPoint slides! While I would 100% go to class, if you happen to miss a day, reading just the slides will have you do well in the class. This semester, Prof. Keller came in and taught a few classes, and I can say with 100% certainty that Weiss is a better teacher. She is easy to follow and truly makes sure you understand the concepts. She also had the TA's host review sessions, which were very helpful for the tests. So if you want a fun, relatable, and easy to follow professor, take this class.

Most of the bad ratings are for Mohan's lab, and the quality of your lab depends on your TA. But Mohan herself is a great lecturer. Really good professor, made the class pretty easy to understand and easy to find success. There is a lab manual that you have to buy (SimBio) and there are graded readings (but they're graded on completion), however you honestly don't need to read the textbook. Mohan only puts material that she goes over in lecture on the exams, and she records all of her lectures, and it was really convenient!

Attendance matters however as she puts random participation questions in the lecture, so you will have to wake up at 9am and go to the lectures, but she drops like 7 of those participation question grades. Use frugally tho! A lot of the other reviews on here talk a lot about the other work she assigns throughout the semester, but it really isn't a lot and fairly easy. There are weekly in-class "quizzes" on Fridays which go over the material that she talked about throughout the week, so even if you do skip you should still keep up with the material. The exams are also fairly similar to the weekly class quizzes so they can help you get an idea of what kind of questions would be on the exam. You can also go to office hours, inbox the TAs, and go to Guided Study Sessions if you need help. GSS sessions are hosted two times a week at the same time.

Overall this course with this professor was fairly easy imo, if you put a little bit of effort into the class you will succeed!

Legit FREAKING AMAZING!!!! She is the best professor I have ever had at UMD. Her class is very easy to follow, and her slides have EVERYTHING you need to know for the tests. She is pretty young, so shes pretty funny and relatable. If you try, and study in this class, you will do well. Also she really does try to learn a ton of peoples names in a huge lecture hall, which is rare. Please take her. I am so glad I did. (she had no reviews when I signed up haha)

I absolutely hated biology before taking this class, the way she teaches the material is so interesting and her exams are EXTREMELY fair if you study what she asks. She provides objectives for every lecture (also records) which compile and make a perfect study guide. Throughout her lectures she will also emphasize material verbally or it will be boxed/bolded on a slide which indicates she is likely going to test the material on the exam.

She cares a lot about her students and her job, she puts genuine effort into prioritizing the needs of the class ie. slowing down on content if needed, answering questions. There are weekly quizzes to check your knowledge and she drops the two lowest of the scores, she also does free participation points every class which is nice. 

The only reason I can think of why someone may not like her is because she had to leave the class for 2-3 weeks due to health related concerns and people were angry that she had another lecturer (keller) step in as well as lectured virtually. HOWEVER, because the class was so thrown off by Keller's lecture style (which in my opinion, hes very nice and sweet and his lectures tell a story, but his slides are not details whatsoever and I felt like falling asleep) she ended up completely removing any material he taught in the midterm AND the exam, all this to say shes EXTREMELY accomodating. 

Additonally, her slides/lectures are detailed enough that you don't need to do any of the additional readings on SimBio if you so please. 

DEFINITELY take her if you can, shes funny, blunt, teaches everyone well, and is super willing to accomodate any needs/questions/concerns. The class is structured so well for such a new professor.

Best professor I have had at UMD hands down!! Really cares about the success for her students and showcases that every single day. I also love that Dr. Weiss is very intentional with getting to know students names which feels so important when you're in a large lecture. She also records her lectures which is so helpful for exam review! The exams are very fair with information coming straight from the slides. I also love that she reiterates important concepts over, and over, and over again to make them stick in your head. Additionally, if you are pre-health she consistently makes applications to the real world that may be interesting to you. She truly is incredible, and I would highly recommend.

He is a nice person overall; however, for this class, he goes very fast over the slides, making it hard to understand the concepts. He tells you something won't be on the exam, but then puts it on the exam. He does not curve, but he does drop the lowest midterm grade, which is nice. The only way I got through was by going to the GSS and asking chat to explain the concepts to me. One time, I asked him to explain a question to me, and he told me it was in the slideshow and told me to study harder.

I don't understand the hate that Dr. Haag is getting. I thought his class was very straightforward. Sometimes the material can get a bit overwhelming but thats kinda just par for the course with biology, there's always a lot of memorization. 

Dr. Haag gives very in depth explanations. I understand that sometimes he rambles and can give wordy explanations but he's always willing to explain in more detail after class or during office hours. You can tell he genuinely enjoys biology and likes to teach/lecture about it. 

Something I really liked about his class were the practice exams. They were very representative of what would be on the exam and often there were questions that were identical between the practice and the real midterm. Another thing that was nice was that he almost never got behind. There were maybe two instances where he lost track of time and content had to be pushed back, however, in each instance he was able to catch us up very fast and leave us with ample time for studying.

I love Dr. Weiss as a person but as a teacher as well. Her slides are very helpful and her exams reflect exactly what was talked about during lecture. All lectures are recorded and so were the ta review sessions. doesn't give that many assignments but the ones given are pretty easy. there are participation questions each lecture. Dr Weiss is EXTREMELY accommodating, as she missed a few weeks due to health issues and because of this removed photosynthesis from the exam and final, and she has a great energy and enthusiasm every class.

Professor Weiss feels like the professor who helps a recent high school graduate transition to college. She acknowledges that not everyone is a biology scientist and explains concepts several times for people to understand.

She is also funny, gives a "sassy aunt vibe", which helps keep the class engaging.  I have sat through class with other BSCI professors, and she was definitely the most entertaining one. The exams also seemed to correspond with the lecture concepts for the most part. Studying will get you a 90% guarantee. 

Nice bonus, she records all of her lectures. I wouldn't skip, though, considering there are participation points.

I absolutely love this man. My friends and I like to call him a big teddy bear because gets giggly and excited about the topics he teaches. His lectures at times could be a little boring but he is very passionate and knowledgeable about biology and tries his best to make sure everyone understands the content. He assigns online homeworks and worksheets every so often that are definitely a grade booster. His exams are completely fair and the study guides he gives are EXACTLY what is covered on the exam, so as long as you study his guides thoroughly you will do well. Overall, love this professor and definitely recommend his class if you can!

He is obviously so smart and is a very nice guy but honestly not a good professor. Speaks to the class like they are colleagues in ways that are hard to understand especially if you are trying to take notes at the same time. Exams are so hard to prepare for because you basically will have to reteach yourself EVERYTHING because he talks to the class like they are biology experts and it is so hard to actually understand. Literally doing the simbio homework assignments helped me learn more than any single one of his lectures. I literally cannot wait for this class too be over. If you can DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WITH HIM.

This class is super easy if you review the slides because ethe exams are based on the slides. The workload is basically nothing just some weekly review quiz and an occasional graded module. Honestly such a good class and very interesting. Dr. Weiss is a great professor and funny too. Just take her class. The exam format is consistent so you know what to be prepared for.

I do think Mohan is a so-so professor overall. She is very nice as a person and I think is welcoming if you need help, want your exam returned etc. But I do think she is a robotic lecturer which can be boring quick and you'll have to review her lecture recordings in all honesty. Sometimes she can be kinda snarky but it's not really that serious. 

You have weekly problem sets due on fridays, participation questions every class (9 are dropped), 3 exams, and a end of the week lecture quiz thats review. I think this is truly the only pro on her class, it's really organized and structured so props to her. This unfortunately does not override how difficult she has molded her exams. 

The exams are directly derived from the lectures, class problem sets, and lecture quizzes. However the real caveat is your exams (the main dictator of your grade) and problem sets are all written out, there is no multiple choice what so ever. This means you must remember the steps, definitions, and essentially I feel like it is not the most forgiving on top of grading. Even if you get the mark they want and happen to over explain, you'll lose points because it is not exact. Meaning you could really know your stuff but potentially missing one mark or a word will lose you an entire section.

She makes the class pretty easy. Fair exams, lots of information on each slide, and its a chill lecture (and sometimes kinda funny). Only problem is that she just reads off of slides, and sometimes lectures are very disorganized. If you want a good grade in the class then take her, but I feel like Im not learning as in depth information as I should for my future bsci classes.

Professor Haag is an extremely passionate and kind person. He is really into biology and his love for it really comes across in lectures. However, his lectures can seem like he is just reading off of a 65 page slideshow everyday, so make sure that you are studying/taking notes in your own time. I'm not sure why his rating is so low because if you just study the content from the slideshows you will do fine on your exams. Also, if you ever email him with a question, he is happy to help and enjoys talking to his students. The one thing is that midterms count for a very large portion of your class and they are never curved (worst midterm is dropped though).

LOVE this professor! Dr. Keller is great and helps so much! 
The grades are mostly the exams, take home quizzes, and in class worksheets that the TAs help you on. The take home quizzes are very similar to the questions on the exams. He also gives extra credit for doing clicker questions. Mostly easy class and if you study you will be fine.

Her exams are very relevant to what she teaches, and all of the homework’s, quizzes, and participation add up to make a pretty fair “grade boost.” Very down to earth and funny. She can be a little blunt, which could sometimes be perceived as condescending. But I’m not exactly neurotypical, so I doubt the vast majority of people would perceive it as such.  I’m on the brink of an A to A-, but I probably could have been basically guaranteed an A if I didn’t overthink on the exam. What I mean by this is that the questions are not made to trick you AT ALL and you should always take them to mean the simplest thing you think it means. 

Overall, she is fair and you can tell she puts time and effort into her lectures. Definitely a safe choice if you need BSCI170.

As someone more into the ecology & evolution side of biology, I wasn't expecting to enjoy this class as much as I did with Dr. Weiss as a professor. Her slides are thorough, organized, easy to read, and she spends a good amount of time explaining the concepts verbally--often in several ways--to ensure understanding.
Her lecture style is engaging, clear, and not super fast-paced (great for me), yet we still get through all of the content each day. She does have 8 lecture quizzes, but they are often online, always open-note, and she drops the lowest 2; it's basically another study tool and grade booster. 

Her exams are harder than Keller's from what I've heard BUT they are very fair. Take the notes, review lecture quizzes, attend the exam reviews, make fairly detailed flashcards (I found this very helpful) and you will be fine. You don't need to put in a lot of hours per week into this class to get an A-/B+. I agree with the other reviews that Keller's lecture style was harder to follow when he stepped in for her absence, and looking back at his slides later did nothing for me either. Something to consider.

Dr. Weiss is a fun, lighthearted, engaging, and passionate professor. The best STEM professor I've had thus far. It's uncommon for a new professor to be this great, and I suspect that she'll only get better. I took 18 credits this semester and her class was my escape from everything else!

such a good professor, I would recommend him if you take BSCI170. I can tell he cares about his students and genuinely wants them to pass. His tests are very fair, definitely not made for you to fail. He posts all his slideshows, but sometimes I couldn't really make sense of some of the stuff on them. Try to listen to how he explains it, or do your own studying on the topic outside of class to better understand it (this is what worked the best for me). It might seem like there are a lot of assignments for this class, but most of them are not very time-consuming and genuinely made to help you practice with the material. Overall such a nice guy and great professor cannot recommend him enough!

Dr. Keller's lectures are veryyyyy hard to stay focused during. They can be annoying and sometimes pointless to attend since he posts all the lectures and slides. The course started off fairly easy however progressively got more content-heavy. As someone who took AP Biology in high school and did well in class and on the exam, I started to struggle towards the end so I can't imagine the level of difficulty for those who did not. I recommend him though, as long as you put in the effort, you should do fine.

If you do not have an AP Bio background, good luck. His lectures are the most useless thing I have ever been to. Casting aside my overwhelming disinterest in the subject, I can admit that Prof. Fletcher is a solid lecturer. Yet some reviewers have overlooked the flaws in his pedagogy, the exam policy, and the lopsided grading scheme. On one hand, he explains vital concepts, diagrams, and terms in an intelligible manner; on the other, he jams so much content into each session that recording notes by hand is not feasible. There are two options in this course: you can either bring a device to class or watch Panopto uploads after the fact. I can only speak for myself when I say that his quantity-over-depth approach has swayed me in favor of the latter. There is no point in attending class other than contributing to group assignments.

While you receive many chances to succeed on exams (there are four in total), the other tasks barely nudge your grade in either direction, and rather than lessening the weight of your poorest exam score, he discards your worst concept check/group activity/SimuText scores instead, underscoring the fact that exams hold a staggering influence over grade calculation in this class. There is no exam curving, and you are also forbidden from using notes when taking exams. If students must be penalized, then it should be for a lack of understanding. It is quite different when students fail to recall one among countless testable pieces of information while three other courses are battling for room in their long-term storage. This unscientific closed-book policy is not specific to BSCI170, but I have to attack it whenever I see it. 

I neither recommend nor advise against taking this class--the positives and negatives level out. Do what you feel.
